name: ch05_society_committee_quorum
alt: A housing society committee of five: three members signed a decision, and asking any three members always reaches at least one signer, while asking only two can miss them all.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves showing the same housing society committee of five members seated in a row behind a long table in a society office, with a framed building photo on the wall. The five members are a retired man in a white kurta with spectacles, a middle-aged woman in a cotton sari, a young man in a polo shirt, an elderly woman with a shawl, and a bearded man in a checked shirt. The first three of them each hold a sheet with a bold green signature tick, showing they signed the decision; the last two hold blank sheets and look unaware. LEFT panel: a young resident in a T-shirt holding a clipboard asks three of the members, shown by three curved arrows from his clipboard to three chairs, and one of the arrows lands on a member with a green tick, so a small green tick bubble pops up over the resident's head: he found the decision. RIGHT panel: the same resident asks only the two members at the far end, the ones with blank sheets, with two curved arrows, and a red question-mark bubble appears over his head because neither of them saw the decision. A small number card on the table in each panel shows the arithmetic: "3 + 3 > 5" on the left and "3 + 2 = 5" on the right. Bright midday office light, calm civic mood. Labels: "ASK 3" above the left panel, "ASK 2" above the right panel.

name: ch05_committee_quorum_cracks
alt: Four small scenes of a housing committee where the three-of-five signing rule still goes wrong: two versions signed at once, a reader asking mid-signing, a torn-out signature left behind, and a file copied from a neighbour.
scene: A four-panel grid, each panel showing a corner of the same housing society office with members of the five-person committee at a table, illustrating one way the sign-three, ask-three rule cracks. TOP LEFT: two committee members, a woman in a sari and a man in a polo shirt, sign two different versions of the same notice at the same moment, one sheet saying paint the gate green and the other blue, shown as two coloured swatches, with a small red spark between the pens. TOP RIGHT: a resident with a clipboard asks a member a question while that member is still halfway through signing, pen mid-stroke, and the resident's speech bubble shows a question mark because the answer depends on the timing. BOTTOM LEFT: a meeting notice with a big red cancelled stamp lies on the table, but two sheets that were already signed sit untouched in a tray beside it, nobody erasing them, a small exclamation badge above the tray. BOTTOM RIGHT: an elderly member whose file was lost leans over to a neighbour's desk and photocopies an old, yellowed file, a calendar on the wall showing that the copy is out of date. Every panel uses the same office furniture so they read as one place. Soft daylight, gently worried mood. Labels: "CONCURRENT" above the top-left panel, "STALE COPY" above the bottom-right panel.

key: Two train coaches reading a running
name: ch05_coach_announcement_lag
alt: A train whose engine has made 1,000 announcements while coach 7 has heard only 940, compared with a crowd passing news in any order where no lag can be counted.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin horizontal line. TOP panel: a long passenger train seen side-on running along a track through green fields, an engine at the left with a driver at a microphone, and a long paper announcement tape coming out of a box in the engine and running along the roof of every coach like a ticker; a counter on the engine shows "1000". Several coaches further back, coach 7, marked with a big number seven on its side, has a ticker counter showing "940", and a passenger leans out of its window with a hand to his ear, trying to hear, while a bracket along the tape between the two counters shows the gap clearly. BOTTOM panel: a busy railway platform with no tape at all, where five passengers, a student with a backpack, a vendor with a basket, an old man with a stick, a mother with a child and a porter in a red shirt, whisper news to each other in a tangle of crossing curved arrows going every which way; above the tangle floats a stopwatch with a big question mark on its face, because nobody can say how far behind anyone is. Bright day for the top panel, crowded busy light on the platform. Labels: "60 BEHIND" over the gap bracket in the top panel, "NO SINGLE TAPE" above the bottom panel.

key: A company with offices in Mumbai and Frankfurt
name: ch05_mumbai_frankfurt_contracts
alt: A Mumbai manager signs off once two of three local contract copies are filed while a courier carries the copy to Frankfurt later, and two filing departments post updates to each other at night.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the left half a Mumbai office with a window showing the sea and palm trees, the right half a Frankfurt office with a window showing pointed rooftops and a cathedral spire. LEFT half: three grey filing cabinets in a row; two clerks, a young woman in a kurta and a young man in a shirt and tie, have just slid copies of the same contract into the first two cabinets, each drawer showing a green tick, while the third drawer is still empty and open. A manager in a blazer stands beside them stamping the contract approved with a big rubber stamp and a satisfied smile, not waiting for the third copy. From the left half, a courier on a scooter with a sealed envelope rides off along a dashed line towards the right half, with a small hourglass over him to show he arrives later. RIGHT half: an identical row of three cabinets with two Frankfurt clerks, one in a sweater and one with a ponytail, waiting for the envelope. At the bottom of the picture, under a night sky with a crescent moon, two small post bags travel along a dashed curve in both directions between the two offices, showing the two filing departments exchanging updates every night. Daylight in both offices, deep blue night strip below. Labels: "2 OF 3 FILED" over the Mumbai cabinets, "LATER" by the courier, "NIGHTLY POST" over the night strip.
